$comment: SITE UI TOKENS — additive to the brand palette, never a replacement for it.
design-systems/exteriors/tokens.json is the BRAND palette. It exists so a rendered social
post looks like Coldstream, and render-post reads it directly. It is authoritative and this
A website needs things a rendered post never does: a success state, an error state, a focus
ring, a disabled control, a form-field border. Those are interface states, not brand colour,
and they have no business in the social render pipeline — a form-validation red should never
be able to reach a composite.
So the flow is one-directional: brand tokens flow INTO the site layer, never the reverse.
If you are tempted to 'fix' the split by merging this into tokens.json, don't — you would be
putting website UI colour into the file that paints every social and print asset.
Accent orange is deliberately NOT reused for success. Accent has exactly one job in this
brand: emphasis, the last word of a headline. Making it also mean 'included' dilutes the
$focus_note: focus intentionally equals the brand accent — a focus ring should be the loudest thing on the page and the brand already owns that colour. It is declared here rather than referenced so a brand change cannot silently weaken an accessibility affordance.
$web_comment: WEB DESIGN LANGUAGE — the second thing this file adds that a composite never needs.
The website and the social renders are two systems, and this block is the boundary. The
social system is Saira Condensed ExtraBold, uppercase, accent #E8843B on #0E1B2A, and it is
locked; it paints every rendered post and it is not what a browser should show. The web
system is a rounded geometric sans in sentence case on a mid navy ground with a light-blue
emphasis, and it governs the four page templates and nothing else.
NEITHER GOVERNS THE OTHER. Do not 'correct' these values to tokens.json, and do not push
them back into it — a change here must never reach a social composite, and a change there
must never restyle a headline in a browser. Colour that both systems share (primary blue,
accent orange, the neutrals) still comes from tokens.css; only what the two genuinely
EVERY VALUE BELOW IS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. They are read off the hero of
public/preview/cincinnati-market-landing.html — the approved prototype. When that page and
the build disagree, the prototype wins and the number is copied, not eyeballed.
$web_note: hero_accent is the headline's emphasis phrase — light blue, not accent orange. Orange is the social system's emphasis and it stays there; on the web hero it sat on a near-black ground and read as a warning, which is what the prototype fixed.
